findings.claim: constraints.md's Release Plan states the v1 wedge as capture 'at source' / 'at creation' in two places, directly contradicting the ratified D-70 restatement that sits six lines away in the same section and is repeated in two sibling meta files. Neither contradicting statement carries a marker; one is explicitly labelled '(unchanged)'.
findings.evidence: constraints.md:199 — 'The irreducible wedge: hire → do the work → capture credit + split at source → on one identity.' AND constraints.md:242-243 — '**Rights nuance (unchanged)**: v1 includes split **capture** (cheap — a signed document at creation, the unrepeatable wedge), NOT royalty **collection**'. Both contradict constraints.md:205 — '| 02 | Credits & Attribution | the wedge — capture at the **first sharing moment** (D-70, 2026-07-22; capture-at-source is the *direction*, not the v1 claim — see § Project Surfaces, Desktop row) | 9 |'; and problem-statement.md:49-51 — 'The honest v1 statement is therefore **"capture at the first sharing moment"**. That is still a structural advantage over reconstruction ... but it is not "present at the moment of creation", and nothing v1 ships may say that it is.'; and competitive-landscape.md:65 — 'the wording must not claim source capture.'
findings.failureScenario: /plan-phase reads constraints.md § Release Plan — which constraints.md:191-192 calls 'the single most important input to /plan-phase' — and slices the v1 domain-09 split-capture work against 'a signed document at creation'. That schedules capture inside the session at the moment the work exists, which requires the 07.09 DAW bridge. constraints.md:292 rules the Desktop surface 'NOT AUTHORISED' and :319 rules that 'DAW close is unavailable as a trigger' in v1, so the sliced work is unbuildable on the authorised surface. The competing reading (line 205) produces a completely different v1 slice: the review link 07.05.02 plus the PWA-push session-close prompt 07.06.02. Two implementers reading independently build two different v1 wedges, and problem-statement.md:38-39 records that an overclaim discovered later 'is an unrecoverable trust breach'.

findings.failureScenario: The file's own downstream contract at :7-9 states '/create-prd (architecture + shared-mechanism registry) ... inherit this file. The **New Cross-Cut Mechanisms** table is the authoritative "extract-me-as-shared" list — anything here must NOT be rebuilt per-domain.' /create-prd therefore commissions the Purchased-Input Clearance Propagation mechanism and must choose push-at-purchase or pull-as-of-at-release to specify it. Those are different architectures (an event emitted at purchase time and stored on the downstream record, versus an as-of query resolved at release time against the purchase ledger), with different failure modes when a purchase is later refunded. No owner is named and no stage is designated to decide, so the stage that hits it first invents the answer silently. Same for whether the practice-tool surface is one shared cross-cut or three education-owned instances.

findings.forcedInvention: How many of the 101 boundary problems are resolved by Section-1 mechanism extraction (~65 or ~85), and what the disposition is of the ~16 that no class accounts for.
findings.claim: The D-17 verdict prose attributes mechanism extraction to '~85 of the 101' while the classification table immediately below attributes it to '~65'; the table's four classes sum to ~85, leaving ~16 of the 101 boundary problems with no class and no resolution.
findings.evidence: cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:239 — '**The fix for ~85 of the 101 is mechanism extraction per Section 1 — not domain merger.**' versus the Classification summary table at :250-253 — '| Clean / defended seams (evidence FOR split) | ~10 | ... | None — leave as-is |', '| Tooling mis-tags (not real seams) | 2 | ... | Suppress spurious rows in assembler |', '| Unowned coordination seams / cross-cut mis-modelled as feature | ~65 | ... | **Extract Section-1 mechanism** |', '| Genuine merge / shared-owner candidates | ~8 | ... | See below |'. Only the ~65 row resolves to extraction; 10 + 2 + 65 + 8 = 85, against the 101 declared at :4-5 ('101 boundary problems (`bp`)') and restated at :227 and :233.
findings.failureScenario: The file's downstream contract at :7-8 names '/decompose-architecture (domain/shard boundaries)' as an inheritor. That stage reads §3 to know which boundary problems are already dispositioned and which still need a shard-boundary decision. It finds two incompatible counts for the extraction class and ~16 boundary problems that appear in the source pool but in no class row and no resolution column. It must invent whether those ~16 are clean seams needing no action, extraction candidates that were missed, or merge candidates — and an unclassified boundary problem that is actually an unowned coordination seam becomes an unowned seam in the shard structure, which is the exact defect §1 exists to prevent.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether the Producer persona's Unique Constraint and Success Criteria veto or qualify the ratified v1 capture surface, given personas.md is consumed by every domain Role Matrix and every feature Role Lens.
findings.claim: personas.md states the Producer's constraints in DAW terms that the ratified v1 surface cannot satisfy — a browser-only capture flow and a session-file-close trigger that constraints.md explicitly rules unavailable in v1 — and personas.md is the only D-70-affected meta file that received no restatement note.
findings.evidence: personas.md:81 — '**Unique Constraint** | Their work happens inside a DAW, not a browser. Any capture flow requiring them to leave the session and go fill in a web form will not be used.' and personas.md:79 — '**Success Criteria** | ... Measurable: split agreed before the session file closes, not after money appears.' Against constraints.md:292 — '**NOT AUTHORISED** (owner decision 2026-07-22, D-70). No WeJammin-installed client software runs on a user's own machine' and constraints.md:319 — 'The close **signal** is likewise limited in v1 — producer tap, booked end and the 72 h backstop apply; DAW close is unavailable as a trigger.' personas.md:4 declares its reach: 'Consumed by: every domain index Role Matrix (24), every feature file Role Lens.' problem-statement.md:36 and competitive-landscape.md:17 both carry an explicit dated D-70 restatement block; personas.md carries none.
findings.failureScenario: A spec writer authoring the Role Lens for 07.06.02 (the v1 session-close capture prompt, delivered by PWA web push + in-app per constraints.md:293) reads the Producer persona — the persona personas.md:71-72 calls 'The capture point. Without this persona the provenance wedge has no mechanism' — and finds its stated constraint that a web-form capture flow 'will not be used', plus a success criterion keyed to a DAW-close event that v1 cannot observe. One writer treats the persona as governing and flags the ratified v1 mechanism as failing its primary persona; another treats D-70 as governing and ignores the persona rows. The two produce different acceptance criteria for the single most load-bearing v1 feature.

findings.claim: Every explicitly-labelled 'Measurable' success metric in the unit is directional — a metric is named but no number, unit or timeframe is attached — and the one numeric target inherited from the predecessor is explicitly demoted to aspiration.
findings.evidence: personas.md:52 — 'Measurable: time-to-book a session drops; credits are cited rather than claimed.'; personas.md:104 — 'Measurable: fewer no-shows; advancing takes minutes; settlement is arithmetic the system already did.'; personas.md:132 — 'Measurable: alert → attendance conversion.'; counterparties.md:50 — 'Measurable: time from brief to executed licence, and the proportion of shortlisted works that clear without escalation.'; counterparties.md:78 — 'Measurable: claims per licensed upload, and time-to-release when one occurs.'; constraints.md:281 — 'the predecessor's "99.9% uptime" claim is aspiration, not a locked budget.'
findings.failureScenario: 'advancing takes minutes' is not testable as written — one implementer reads it as a sub-5-minute advance flow and budgets a single-screen advance sheet; another reads 'minutes rather than days' and accepts a 40-minute multi-step flow as satisfying it. Neither reading can be falsified against the text. Note in mitigation: the engineering performance budget is tracked to a named stage (constraints.md:273 'Hard budget set at /create-prd-compile'), so this finding is scoped to the product-success metrics, which have no such deferral marker and no owner.

findings.failureScenario: /create-prd builds the shared-mechanism registry against the ratified D-27 figure of 52 mechanisms, reconciles it to a 54-row table, and must decide which two rows are surplus — or, more likely, assumes the deltas are dedup noise and does not notice that seven feature rows (83 vs 76) are likewise unaccounted. Because §1 is declared at :9 as 'the authoritative "extract-me-as-shared" list — anything here must NOT be rebuilt per-domain', an entry silently dropped during that reconciliation is rebuilt per-domain, which is the precise failure the section exists to prevent.
